articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Issues ICC General Licenses, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics. Concurrently, OFAC issued new General Licenses related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and removed a designation related to Burma.

The settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions programs. The specific details of the violations and the terms of the settlement are outlined in the enforcement information released by OFAC.

The issuance of General Licenses concerning the ICC and the removal of a Burma-related designation reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy in response to evolving geopolitical considerations and humanitarian concerns.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the issuance of a new General License pertaining to Russia-related sanctions. This action aims to authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing sanctions programs.

General Licenses are frequently used by OFAC to provide clarity and allow for specific activities to proceed, often to facilitate humanitarian aid, certain financial transactions, or other activities deemed consistent with U.S. foreign policy objectives.
The details of the newly issued General License specify the scope of authorized activities and any conditions or limitations that apply to transactions involving Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Issues General Licenses for Iran and Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting entities and individuals involved in Iran-related activities. These designations are part of ongoing efforts to exert pressure on the Iranian regime.

In conjunction with the new Iran-related designations, OFAC also issued a new Iran-related General License, which typically authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited. Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License has been amended, indicating adjustments to the scope of authorized activities concerning Russia.

These actions underscore the U.S. government's dynamic approach to sanctions, utilizing both restrictive measures and targeted authorizations to achieve its foreign policy and national security objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designation Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designation removals and updates to its sanctions lists. These changes reflect ongoing reviews of sanctions targets and adjustments based on new information or policy considerations.

In a significant development, OFAC also published an Iran-related Alert, warning foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted without advance notification if they continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions. This alert is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' launched in August 2026 to cut off financial resources supporting the Iranian regime.

Furthermore, an Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) has been amended, specifically FAQ 156, which now removes language indicating that OFAC would generally contact foreign financial institutions before making a finding of sanctionable activity. This change signals a heightened potential for immediate sanctions targeting without prior warning for institutions with exposure to Iranian banks.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism sanctions program. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist organizations or engaging in terrorism-related activities.

These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks of terrorist groups and prevent them from accessing the international financial system. The U.S. government continues to prioritize counter-terrorism efforts through economic sanctions.

The specific details of the designated parties and the reasons for their inclusion on the sanctions list are provided in the official OFAC announcement, reinforcing the U.S. commitment to combating global terrorism.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and Updates, Designates Transnational Criminal Organization, and Publishes Iran-Related Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing designations, targeting entities and individuals involved in activities contrary to U.S. national security interests. These actions are part of a broader strategy to counter the Iranian regime's illicit activities.

In a separate action, OFAC also designated a Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), aiming to disrupt its financial operations and illicit networks. This highlights OFAC's commitment to combating various forms of illicit finance.

Furthermore, OFAC published an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ), providing additional guidance and clarification on the scope and application of Iran sanctions. These publications are crucial for compliance by financial institutions and other entities.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations sanctions programs. These actions target individuals and entities involved in supporting terrorism and engaging in illicit transnational criminal activities.

Concurrently, OFAC has removed several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya. These removals indicate a recalibration of sanctions policies in these areas, potentially reflecting changes in behavior or diplomatic considerations.
The dual actions of new designations and removals demonstrate OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, continuously adjusting its lists to address evolving threats and policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a series of new designations across multiple sanctions programs, including Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation. These actions target a broad spectrum of illicit activities and threats to U.S. national security.

The designations aim to disrupt the financial networks of drug traffickers, terrorist organizations, and those involved in proliferation activities, as well as entities supporting the Iranian regime. This comprehensive approach underscores the U.S. commitment to combating various global threats.
These actions reinforce the U.S. government's resolve to use its economic tools to counter illicit actors and safeguard the international financial system from abuse.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, Cuba Sanctions Regulations, New and Amended Cuba-Related FAQs, and Cuba-Related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced significant updates to its Cuba sanctions program, including the publication of new regulatory amendments. These amendments aim to refine and clarify the existing restrictions on transactions involving Cuba.

In conjunction with the regulatory changes, OFAC has also published comprehensive Cuba Sanctions Regulations, providing a consolidated and updated framework for compliance. This is complemented by the issuance of new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), offering further guidance to the public.

Additionally, OFAC has released a Cuba-related Alert, which likely highlights specific risks or compliance considerations for individuals and entities engaging in activities related to Cuba. These actions collectively underscore the ongoing U.S. policy towards Cuba and the importance of adherence to sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the issuance of amended General Licenses pertaining to Venezuela. These amendments modify existing authorizations for certain transactions and activities involving Venezuela, which would otherwise be prohibited under U.S. sanctions.

The adjustments to Venezuela-related General Licenses often reflect shifts in U.S. foreign policy objectives or responses to developments within Venezuela. Such amendments can impact various sectors, including humanitarian aid, oil, and financial services.
Entities and individuals engaging in Venezuela-related transactions are advised to review the amended General Licenses carefully to ensure ongoing compliance with OFAC regulations.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
